title: Dynamic priority fee is p75 of the GLOBAL fee distribution, not the accounts being contended — it underbids on exactly the hot pump.fun races it exists to win
evidence: getRecentP75() calls this.getConnection().getRecentPrioritizationFees() with NO lockedWritableAccounts argument (priorityFeeService.ts:39). The RPC therefore returns the network-wide recent fee sample; nonZero-p75 of that (line 41) is dominated by ordinary/idle traffic across all programs. The computed fee is then clamped to [floorSol, min(maxPriorityFeeSol=0.005, 5% position)] (getPriorityFeeSol lines 60-67). dynamicPriorityFee is ON in the shipped build (featureFlags.ts:138 PACKAGED_DEFAULTS) and this fee is used for BOTH sniper and copy trades via executeRealMainnetTrade (sniperEngine.ts:1465-1476). getRecentPrioritizationFees accepts an array of writable accounts to scope the percentile to what winners actually paid to touch those accounts; that argument is unused, so the estimate is blind to the specific mint / bonding-curve / pump.fun-program contention.
impact: On a contended launch or fast copy entry, the accounts everyone is racing carry fees far above the global p75; the diluted global p75 lands near the static floor (0.001) instead of near the 0.005 ceiling, so the order underpays and loses the inclusion race — a worse or missed fill on precisely the trades where fee competitiveness decides the outcome. Estimated magnitude: the difference between a floor-ish ~0.001 SOL bid and a competitive ~0.005 SOL bid during bursts, i.e. losing races the ceiling could have won.
proposed_fix: Pass the contended writable accounts to getRecentPrioritizationFees (the pump.fun program, the bonding-curve PDA for the mint, and/or the mint account) so the p75 reflects fees paid to touch those accounts; keep the global sample only as a fallback. Alternatively raise the percentile (p90) or the ceiling for buys. Keep the 10s cache but key it per-account-set.
verdict_reason: Verified. getRecentP75 calls getRecentPrioritizationFees() with no lockedWritableAccounts argument (priorityFeeService.ts:39), so the sample is network-wide; nonZero p75 of that (40-41) is diluted by idle/ordinary traffic across all programs. getPriorityFeeSol converts and clamps via clampPriorityFeeSol = max(floorSol, min(computedSol, ceilingSol, 5%*position)) (priorityFeeService.ts:60-67; pipelineUtils.ts:106). dynamicPriorityFee is ON in the packaged build (featureFlags.ts:138, listed in INTENDED_PACKAGED_DIVERGENCE at 162) and the fee feeds BOTH sniper and copy trades through executeRealMainnetTrade (sniperEngine.ts:1465-1476; copy path routes here via 4050). On a contended launch the accounts everyone races carry fees well above global p75, so the diluted estimate lands near the static floor instead of near the cap — on exactly the inclusion races the feature exists to win. Medium is honest and appropriately bounded: because of the max(floorSol,...) clamp the dynamic fee never bids BELOW the legacy static fee (so this is a missed optimization, not a regression), and for small positions the 5%-of-position cap pins the fee near the floor regardless of the estimator, so the 0.001-vs-0.005 gap only fully materializes for positions >= ~0.1 SOL.

title: RugCheck reads are serialized through one global 500ms rate-limit chain with no cache and no priority lane — a migration (the trade we'd actually take) queues behind every create it will never buy
evidence: enforceRateLimit() chains every request through a single instance-wide rateLimitChain enforcing rateLimitMs=500 min spacing (rugcheckService.ts:39,45,57-66). There is no response cache anywhere in the service. In the entry hot path, EVERY incoming token calls at least getReport (sniperEngine.ts:1948-1953: getReport for non-tradeable creates, getReportWithHolders for migrations/watchlist), and getReportWithHolders issues up to 3 sequential getReport calls with 1200ms gaps (rugcheckService.ts:115-123). Ordering is FIFO with no priority for the migration read. Prior audit flagged this exact shape (docs/research/audit-2026-08-09-architecture-rug-entry-exit.md:162 item 2b: 'global 200ms serial rate-limit chain, no per-mint cache, no priority lane ... a migration queues behind creates it was never going to buy').
impact: During a launch burst (prior data: 18.3% of inter-arrival gaps <200ms, up to 8 in flight), a migration's holder read waits behind N creates at 500ms each before its first attempt, then pays its own 3x500ms + 2x1200ms holder-retry budget. That adds ~2-5s of pure queue latency to the migration entry path — the bot's main strategy and its most time-sensitive entry (token just graduated, price moving). No caching also re-fetches on watchlist re-screens.
proposed_fix: Add a short-TTL per-mint cache (creates re-screened from the watchlist and duplicate deliveries then cost nothing) and a priority lane so tradeable-candidate reads (getReportWithHolders) jump ahead of fire-and-forget create screening in the rate-limit chain.
verdict_reason: Verified in rugcheckService.ts. enforceRateLimit() chains every request through the single instance-wide rateLimitChain (line 39, 57-66) at rateLimitMs=500 (line 45); the promise chain is FIFO with no priority lane. Read the whole 267-line file: there is no response cache of any kind. getReportWithHolders (115-123) does up to 3 sequential getReport calls with 1200ms gaps. In the hot path, sniperEngine.ts:1948-1953 calls getReport (non-tradeable creates) or getReportWithHolders (migration/watchlist) UNCONDITIONALLY for every token reaching processIncomingToken — I checked 1858-1953 and there is no venue/phase early-return before the rugcheck call, so every non-launchSnipe token consumes a 500ms slot ahead of a queued migration read. The queue math (N creates × 500ms + the migration's own 3×500ms + 2×1200ms holder budget) is accurate. status_vs_prior_audit: still_open (the no-cache/no-priority shape flagged in the 2026-08-09 audit persists in the current tree). Severity Medium is honest: real, bounded entry-path latency, no fund loss or bricking; note this affects only the sniper lane (RugCheckService has no copy-path caller), but the finding does not overstate that.

title: Every real buy and sell pays a PumpPortal /api/trade-local HTTP build round-trip on the hot path (localTxBuild off in the shipped build), with a 10s timeout and no fallback
evidence: executeRealMainnetTrade builds the transaction by POSTing to https://pumpportal.fun/api/trade-local (sniperEngine.ts:1534-1558, timeout 10000ms), deserializing the returned bytes, signing, then sendRawTransaction (1569).
